correctness.rationale: For one or two prescribed vertex-pair equalities, the contracting bijection gives probabilities p=S(n-1,k)/S(n,k) and q=S(n-2,k)/S(n,k), even for adjacent pairs. Expanding the two n-1 edge sums proves the exact identity. Strict fixed-k Stirling log-concavity establishes p^2>q; the nonnegative variance of all N=binom(n,2) pair equality indicators forces tau<=2(n-1)/n<2. The n-1 block boundary makes tau=2(n-1)/n and shows sharpness. The k=2 formula shows one overlap can be positive. Exact independent enumerations of partitions to n=6, representatives of each overlap, and exact Stirling threshold checks to n<35 passed; these do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: This solves a natural dependence question for two distinct spanning-tree probes of a single uniformly random k-clustering with a uniform all-n all-k geometric threshold. Disjoint probes correlate negatively while sharing two edges forces positive covariance; exactly one shared edge has genuine parameter-dependent reversal. The count two is sharp, evidenced by all (n-1)-block partitions. The complete covariance depends only on overlap rather than tree shapes, giving a reusable structural invariant.
